title: Anatomy: how a board gets on screen
goal: Understand how a board file written by an agent becomes an interactive map, and where your own notes are kept.

includes: Opening, checking, and showing a board file
Where notes and card positions are kept
excludes: Parts that are not built yet are described as planned, not as working code

groups.label: Outside the app
groups.description: Things the app reads but does not control.

groups.label: Browser app
groups.description: Code that runs in the browser tab.

groups.label: Browser storage
groups.description: Data kept by this browser on this computer.

components.label: Your agent
components.summary: An existing coding agent that you ask to explain a plan or feature. It writes a board file.
inputs: Material you allow it to read

components.label: Board file
components.summary: A JSON document that lists parts, connections, open questions, and scenarios.
components.explanation: The file is **data only**. The app never runs anything from it, and file paths in it are shown as text.
inputs: Written by an agent or a person

components.label: Validator
components.summary: Checks the file's shape, IDs, and references, and rejects a broken file with a clear message.
components.explanation: A rejected file never replaces the board that is already open.
outputs: A checked board, or a list of problems

components.label: Canvas
components.summary: Draws the parts as movable cards and the connections as labeled arrows.

components.label: Inspector
components.summary: Explains the selected part or connection in plain English, with its source label.

components.label: Your notes
components.summary: Your notes, questions, manual arrows, and card positions, kept apart from the agent's explanation.
components.explanation: Keeping your work in a separate layer means an updated board file does not overwrite it.

components.label: Browser storage
components.summary: Keeps boards and your notes in this browser, so they survive a reload.
outputs: The same data after a reload

items.text: The exact rules for keeping notes when an updated board file is opened are not designed yet.
Browser data can be cleared, so an exported file is the only safe backup.

steps.caption: Your agent writes a board file.
You open the file. The validator checks it.
The canvas draws the map, using any positions you saved earlier.
You click a card, and the inspector explains it.
You open a file with a connection that points at a part that does not exist.
The validator lists the problem and stops. The board that was already open stays on screen.
